questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I specifically looked for schools that had courses with sociology of religion and were in the Erasmus program but also, specifically for the destination, that it was located in a Muslim-majority country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't have a bad experience, and I don't regret going but I was very busy with school and handling the bureaucratic things that follows with moving to a country outside of the EU, like the residence permit, which left less time for social experiences than I had imagined. But I ultimately went on exchange for academic opportunities, which was fulfilled.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not that easy, their website is not always up to date.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None. They arranged an online meeting before arrival, but there was not actual assistance upon arrival. Though it seems to have changed now.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was not bad, but I would have been more confident in the beginning if the orientation had been more thorough and not only online.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, there are many facebook groups to join.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Know that it's normal to pay a month's rent in commission when finding an apartment, so save up for this.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very frustratring process.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I'm sorry I cannot.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You get assigned to a whatsapp group of turkish students who will answer questions about it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Some of them ended up not existing when I arrived. Then there are some that I wanted to join but couldn't because only students from that specific department could. Also, a big and important part of the process is to write emails to the professors and ask to be enrolled in their classes. This was very new to me, but you have to kind of beg to be enrolled, explain why the course is important to you, etc.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep calm, you will get enrolled in some courses although it might not be the ones you originally dreamed about. Also, if you don't get them in the first try, there is a second registration round a few weeks later, where you in the meantime can go and ask permission to the professors in person, which might get you into the course. This is normal and expected praxis at Bogazici.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As the BA in Denmark is 3 years and the BA in Turkey is 4 years, it can be a bit difficult to find out which courses are adequate for your level. Both my easiest and hardest courses were 3rd year courses, so you really have no idea, but looking at the syllabuses thoroughly can give a good hint.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different, at least to the sociology department at UCPH. In Copenhagen I only have big lectures with 60+ students in auditoriums. At Bogazici most of the courses are in smaller classes with between 15-40 students. Also attendance and active participation is mandatory and will affect your grade. It is thus more comparable to the danish "gymnasium". But personally I learned way quicker and I appreciated the more personal relationship you get to the professor, where they actually know your name, compared to the danish system.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Sociology of religion
- World Environmental History
- Politics and society in The Middle East 
- Social Anthropology 
- History of social and political thought 
- Pilates

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Although being very challenging, I recommend the course Sociology of Religion, as it is a rare chance of having this type of course, a "seminar". Here we sat around a big table with the professor and together discussed and analyzed the weekly texts. I felt very privileged to have such an interesting course. Also, I strongly recommend the course "World environmental history" if you have the opportunity to be taught by professor Faisal Husain.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There are quite a lot of costs associated with attaining the residence permit. You have to pay for a 1-year turkish insurance + to get your rental contract notarized and translated + pay for getting professional ID pictures taken + pay for registering as a tax payer (even though you are not going to pay taxes). I don't know excatly how much I used in total on the residence permit application, but at least 2500 DKK. .

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Prices are getting insane in Istanbul, so don't expect it to be inexpensive. But the schools cafeteria which serves 3 meals a day is VERY cheap. It costs around 6 DKK for a meal. I highly recommend saving some money by eating here.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I don't think you can ask for more, they have every possible activity - although some of the ones I wanted to join required you to speak turkish.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have an abundance of clubs: sports, knitting, dancing, political, cooking, climbing!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really recommend that you join the clubs, it's here you will meet people and also through the clubs that parties at the universities are thrown.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend going on at least two trips. I went to Fethiye with the Bogazici Erasmus club and to cappadocia with ESI (Erasmus sports istanbul). I recommend that you follow ESI on instagram, they have many activities every week.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs and go out and drink tea with them on the breaks in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I am not sure how much I can express here, but the political climate is obviously very different than in Denmark. It's both way more present in your daily life, while at the same time not being something that people talk openly about. I would not advise against going to Turkey because of this, but I wish I had had a deeper understanding of how it affects university students. I advice, that if you're choosing Turkey as your destination of exchange, then talk to students who have done the same, to learn about the lived experiences of the politcal climate.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Many parts, but especially the street animals everywhere, also in classrooms! (Probably not the place for you if you're allergic) and of course the food! I highly recommend trying the dessert "Künefe".

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The campus is beautiful, you will spend excessive time on public transport, and don't stress too much about grades. The professors go easy on exchange students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Yes, try to plan your schedule so you have some lunch breaks at campus. It's where a lot of the social interaction takes place.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That I grew academically a lot and got to go beyond the euro-centric perspectives I've learned at UCPH.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To have time to socialize and go on adventures - I had a hard time with the required attendance and weekly assignments after being used to the way university is in Denmark.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
